title: Journey - Five Days of Peace - Day 3: Peace that guards

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Peace. <short pause> This is day three, Peace That Guards. <short pause> So far we have two steps. <short pause> Palms up, here it is. <short pause> Shoulders down, it's Yours. <short pause> Today's step turns worry around, until it becomes a conversation.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Come as you are. <short pause> If your mind is busy, it can be busy in here. <short pause> Let your feet or your back find something solid. <short pause> And for one breath, pay attention only to the nearest thing to you... <short pause> the cloth on your skin, the air by your face. <short pause> Something is already very close.

Have you noticed whom we talk to when we worry? <short pause> Usually, it's ourselves. <short pause> We talk about the problem. <short pause> We talk about the people in it. <short pause> We hold whole meetings about tomorrow, and God is the subject of some of them. <short pause> But being talked about... is very different from being talked to.

Paul was a prisoner when he wrote to his friends in Philippi. <short pause> Just before his famous words about worry, he slips in one short sentence. <short pause> The Lord is at hand. <short pause> At hand... near enough to touch. <short pause> Everything that follows rests on that. <short pause> It is in chapter four, verses six and seven.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. <short pause> And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: To be careful, in older English, was to be full of care. <short pause> So this is no scolding for anxious people. <short pause> It is more like a friend touching your arm while you mutter, and saying... He's right here. <short pause> You can say that to Him.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: Let's try it with one worry. <short pause> First, say it the usual way, about. <short pause> What if I can't manage this? <short pause> Now turn, and say it to. <short pause> Lord, will You help me manage this? <short pause> Do you feel the small difference? <short pause> The trouble is the same size. <short pause> But there are two of you in the room.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now use your own. <short pause> Take the sentence that has been circling, and begin it with His name. <short pause> Lord... <short pause> and then ask for exactly what you need. <short pause> Help me sleep. Help me wait. Help me make the call. <short pause> Make it as small and as honest as you like.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And before you leave that request with Him, add two words that look backward. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> For being at hand. <short pause> For one time He has helped you before. <short pause> For hearing this, before you know how He will answer. <short pause> You don't need a long list. <short pause> One true thank You will do.

parts.style: tender reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: Then Paul makes a promise. <short pause> Peace will keep you. <short pause> He doesn't say that you will keep the peace, gripping it tightly all day. <short pause> It does the guarding. <short pause> It can stand watch over a mind that still has questions... <short pause> and over a heart that understands very little of what is going on.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Here is our third step, with the others. <short pause> Palms up... here it is. <short pause> Shoulders down... it's Yours. <short pause> And now, a hand resting on your heart, where His peace keeps watch... <short pause> help me, and thank You. <short pause> If you never learn another step, these three are a whole prayer. <short pause> Here it is. <short pause> It's Yours. <short pause> Help me, and thank You.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Let's pray. <short pause> Lord Jesus, You are nearer than the thing I fear. <short pause> I have talked about it long enough, so now I am talking to You. <short pause> Help me, in the very place I named. <short pause> Thank You for hearing. <short pause> And set Your peace around my heart and mind, until I understand, and even if I don't. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: warm, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: Whenever you catch yourself talking about the worry today, turn one sentence around. <short pause> Put His name at the front, and thanks at the end. <short pause> You have what you need for this, and you can return to these three steps as often as you like. <short pause> Go in peace... <short pause> He is at hand.
